NCB F.No.48/1/12/2023/NCB/MDS filed by the Narcotics Control
Bureau before the learned Special Court for NDPS Act Cases,
Pudukottai, Tamil Nadu, for the offences punishable under
Section 8(c) read with Sections 20(b)(ii)(C), 25, 27(A), 28
and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances
Act, 1985. The High Court, vide the impugned order dated
23.10.2025, dismissed the bail petition of the appellants.
Aggrieved, the appellants are before this Court. 
3. We have heard the learned Senior Counsel appearing
for the parties and perused the material placed on record. 
4. It is not in dispute that accused No(s). 1, 2 and 5
are already on bail and accused No.6 is absconding.  
5. Suffice it to state that the appellants herein have

years three months and the trial would take considerable
time to conclude.

opinion that continued incarceration of the appellants, is
not required.

23.10.2025 passed by the High Court in CRL.OP(MD)No.14846
OF 2025, stands set aside and the appellants shall be
granted  bail  on  the  terms  and  conditions  to  the

terms.

record warranting its reconsideration.

on the ground of delay as well as on merits.

2. The present petition calls in question the correctness of
the order dated 06-07-2026 in CRMM No. 29877/2026 passed by the
High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh. By the said
order, the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner was
rejected in connection with Case/FIR No.77 of 2026 dated
24.03.2026 registered at Police Station Ballabhgarh Sadar,
District Faridabad, Haryana under Sections 351(2), 329(4),
318(4) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
3. When the matter came up for hearing on 07.08.2026, while
issuing notice, this Court had granted interim anticipatory
bail to the petitioner.
4. It is not disputed that the petitioner had appeared
before the concerned Investigating Officer.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the case
has civil overtones; that the petitioner is the  bona fide
purchaser for value without notice; that the petitioner had
filed a suit on 21.02.2026 before the concerned Court seeking
permanent mandatory injunction against the defacto-complainant;
that the FIR lodged on 24.03.2026 is subsequent to the suit;
that  the  petitioner  is  innocent  and  has  been  falsely
implicated.
6. Learned counsel for the State and the defacto-complainant
vehemently deny the submissions of the learned counsel for the
petitioner.
7. Learned counsel for the defacto-complainant submits that
there is discrepancies in the agreement filed with the police
as well as in the suit concerned.

## Page 828

3
8. Having considered the overall facts and circumstances of
the case, we are inclined to confirm the order dated 07.08.2026
granting interim anticipatory bail to the petitioner on the
same terms.
9. With the above observations, the special leave petition
is disposed of.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed
of.

for the defacto-complainant.
2. The present petition calls in question the correctness of
the order dated 25-08-2026 in CRMM No. 47540/2026 passed by the
High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh. By the said
order, the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner was
rejected  in  connection  with  FIR  No.0079  dated  13.10.2025
registered with Police Station Hajipur, District Hoshiarpur,
Punjab, for the offences punishable under Sections 115(2),
118(1), 333, 351(2) & 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
(for short, ‘BNS’)and under Section 118(2) of BNS added later
during investigation.
3. When the matter came up for hearing on 07.09.2026, while
issuing notice, this Court had granted interim protection to
the petitioner.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that this is a
case and counter case inasmuch as the petitioner has also on
14.10.2025 registered FIR No.80/2025. The FIR in question in
the present case is dated 13.10.2025, namely, FIR No.0079/2025.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the co-accused
-Pratap Kumar, against whom the allegation of similar nature
that the similar weapon, namely,  datar was made, has been
enlarged on anticipatory bail and the State has not challenged
the said order.
5. Learned AAG appearing for the State does not dispute that
after  granting  interim  protection  to  the  petitioner,  the
petitioner had appeared before the concerned Investigating
Officer. Learned AAG vehemently opposes the prayer for bail of

3
the  petitioner.  Learned  AAG  submits  that  as  far  as  FIR
No.80/2025, lodged by the petitioner, is concerned, inquiry
revealed that no case is made out and it is on the verge of
being closed. Insofar as the parity claim is concerned, learned
AAG submits that the injury attributed to accused-Pratap Kumar
was simple in nature. 
6. Learned counsel for the complainant, drawing attention to
the inquiry report conducted with regard to the veracity of the
allegations in FIR 80/2025 is concerned, submits that the
inquiry was found that the said FIR was lodged to exert
pressure on the defacto-complainant.
7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the
case, we are inclined to confirm the order dated 07.09.2026
granting interim protection to the petitioner on the same
terms.

is disposed of.

25.03.2026 along with a large number of civil appeals. In
para 9 of the order dated 25.03.2026, this Court directed
the State of Odisha to complete the exercise as directed
by the High Court within a period of six months.

have filed separate Miscellaneous Applications seeking
extention of time to complete the process in one civil
1

appeal at a time.
3. Initially we had granted the time as sought for by
the State of Odisha.
4. But this process cannot go on ad infinitum by filing
separate applications in each of the disposed of civil
appeals.  For  example,  in  the  present  Miscellaneous
Application the prayer has been made to grant 8 weeks’
time  for  completion  of  the  verification  exercise  in
Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.12531 of 2026.
5. While we grant the time as sought for by the State of
Odisha, we make it clear that henceforth i.e., from today
onwards no further Miscellaneous Applications in any of
the connected civil appeals shall be entertained.
6. We grant eight weeks’ time from today as last and
final chance to the State of Odisha to complete the
exercise.
7. Miscellaneous Application is disposed of.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We do not approve the High Court passing interim orders of
this nature which are virtually in the nature of granting final
relief. Facts revealed that the State Government has not granted no
objection certificate (NOC) and in fact, the State has issued a
1 of 2

## Page 979

Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No(s).  39689-39690/2026
moratorium which is continuing. Further, the Pharmacy Council of
India has not granted the approval. Under these circumstances
granting of interim orders are uncalled for. However, in the facts
and circumstances of the case, as the orders impugned are of
07.09.2026 & 21.09.2026 and we are informed by the respondent(s)
that one student has already been admitted, we are not inclined to
interfere with the impugned interim orders passed by the High
Court. We would, however, request the High Court to take up and
dispose of the Writ Petition expeditiously. 
2. Needless to say, admission of any student will be subject to
the outcome of the Writ Petition. 
3. With the aforesaid observation, the Special Leave Petitions
stand disposed of. 
4. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

1. Delay condoned.

1

## Page 1051

record, we are of the view that no error, not to speak of
any error of law could be said to have been committed by
the High Court in dismissing the Criminal Appeal preferred
by the petitioner and thereby affirming the judgment and
order of conviction passed by the Trial Court, holding the
petitioner guilty of the alleged offence.
3. However, taking into consideration the fact that the
petitioner-convict is undergoing life imprisonment past 20
years and 10 months, we permit the petitioner to prefer an
appropriate  representation  addressed  to  the  competent
authority of the State Government, praying for remission of
sentence.
4. If any such representation is preferred, the competent
authority shall look into the same expeditiously and take
appropriate decision, having regard to the remission policy
of the State Government prevailing on the date of the
commission of the alleged crime or any other remission
policy that may be more beneficial to the petitioner-
convict.
5. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands
disposed of.
6. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.

by the defendant under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of
Civil Procedure, 1908 and had rejected the plaint.

Trial Court and has restored the suit.

3. When this order came to be challenged before us by

settlement.

Naidu, learned Senior counsel for the petitioner-
defendant submits that mediation has failed.
5. While in an appropriate case, the scope certainly
of the notice can certainly be enlarged, we are not
persuaded to do so in a case of this nature.
6. As observed by the High Court, the Trial Court
shall proceed with the suit, uninfluenced by the
orders passed by the Trial Court as well as by the
High Court. All contentions are kept open.
7. Subject to the above, the Special Leave Petition
is dismissed.

disposed of.

February, 2027.

The  present  matter  arises  out  of  a  suo-motu  proceeding
initiated against Mr. Digvijay Singh, Group Captain, PS-I, to
explain as to why he has written directly to the Court seeking
clarification with regard to an order passed by this Court on
29.05.2026 in SLP(Crl.) No.9925 of 2026 without moving a proper

## Page 1133

2
application through his learned counsel.
2. Today, Mr. Digvijay Singh, Group Captain, PS-I, is present in
Court and has also filed an affidavit tendering unconditional and
unqualified apology for such act.
3. Besides  tendering  unconditional  and  unqualified  apology,
Mr. Digvijay Singh, Group Captain, PS-I, has admitted that the same
should not have been done and he has realised that it was
impermissible. It has further been undertaken that in future, if
any such a situation arises where any clarification of an order of
any Court is sought, it shall be by way of an appropriate
application moved through the counsel.
4. We are glad to know that Mr. Digvijay Singh, Group Captain,
PS-I, has fairly accepted his mistake and has tendered apology.
5. Accordingly,  accepting  the  unconditional  and  unqualified
apology of Mr. Digvijay Singh, Group Captain, PS-I, the issue
stands consigned. The personal appearance of Mr. Digvijay Singh,
Group Captain, PS-I, stands dispensed with.
6. The present petition stands closed.

ZILA BAR ASSOCIATION UDHAM SINGH NAGAR             Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF UTTARAKHAND & ANR.                        Respondent(s)
[IA No. 349736/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING AND IA No.
349737/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.]
 
Date : 23-11-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE B.V. NAGARATHNA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJEEV SACHDEVA
For Petitioner(s) :Ms. Mrinal Kanwar- 3163, AOR
                   Ms. Sonakshi Malhan, Adv.
                   Mr. Vaibhav Rajsingh Rathore, Adv.
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Despite there being a delay of 893 days in filing the Special
Leave Petition, we have heard learned counsel for the petitioner at
length and we have perused the material on record.
2. We fail to understand as to how the petitioner-Bar Association
could be aggrieved by the Notification dated 17.11.2022 issued by
the High Court of Uttarakhand. The said Notification is in the
interest of the litigant public and for the convenience of the
administration of justice. Placing reliance on the Bengal, Agra and
1

## Page 1405

Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887 and particularly Section 21 of the
said Act, at this stage may not be appropriate.
3. Having regard to access to justice in the Taluka headuarters
also Additional District Judges are posted where they exercise
jurisdiction at par with the District Judges.
4. Such being the case, the litigant public have to file cases at
the jurisdictional level itself rather than filing the cases before
the Courts of Principal District Judge at the District Headquarter
and thereafter, the cases being made over to the Courts of
Additional District Judge either by the District headquarter or at
the Taluka Level.
5. In these circumstances, we dismiss this Special Leave Petition
on the ground of delay as well as on merits.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand dismissed.
 
    (DEEPANSHU)                                (DIVYA BABBAR)
SENIOR PERSONAL ASSISTANT                     COURT MASTER (NSH)

out.

of delay as well as on merits.

dated 09.11.1981, registered at Police Station Ughaiti,
Sahaswan, Uttar Pradesh, for the offences punishable under
Sections 147, 308, 323 and 324 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, and have been sentenced to undergo seven years of
rigorous imprisonment, out of which they have already
undergone twelve months.
3.  Learned counsel for the appellants, at the outset,
has informed this Court that appellants are aged about 85
years  and  there  is  every  possibility  of  their  clean
acquittal. He has also drawn attention of this Court
towards the statement of witnesses. On the other hand,
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Uttar Pradesh
has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
4.     This Court after going through the record and after
hearing learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view
advance age of the both the appellants is of the opinion
that the prayer for suspension of sentence deserves to be
allowed and it is allowed accordingly.
5.  The appellants herein shall be released on bail
during the pendency of the appeal, subject to such terms
and conditions as may be imposed by the Trial Court.
6. Let records of the Courts below be requisitioned.
Upon receipt thereof, soft copies of the same shall be
supplied to the learned counsel for the parties.
7. List the matters for hearing in due course.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We have heard the learned Senior counsel appearing for the
petitioner and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents. 
In our considered view, this is a fit case to quash the

## Page 1569

2
impugned judgment of the High Court, as it not only went against
the earlier order passed by this Court, but also against the very
scheme of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children)
Act, 2015. 
However, we do not want to proceed further, in view of the
subsequent  development  by  which  the  Trial  Court,  by  placing
reliance upon the ossification test, has held that the private
respondent was an adult at the relevant point of time.
Accordingly, with the aforesaid observations, the Special
Leave Petition stands disposed of with the further observation that
the impugned judgment shall not enure to the benefit of the private
respondent. 
Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

1. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties and on perusal
of the impugned order, we are of the considered view that non-appointment of
the Respondent No.1 was on the ground of valid and probable defence that
came to be raised by the petitioner. Hence, no fault can be laid at the doors of
the petitioner for the delay in appointing the writ petitioner/applicant by way of
re-employment.

## Page 1587

2.  Hence, the direction issued under the impugned order to the petitioner to
pay interest on back wages @6% per annum would be too harsh and to that
extent we set aside the same and sustain the impugned order in all other
aspects. Arrears shall be paid expeditiously and at any rate within an outer limit
of eight weeks from today.
3. With this observation, the Special Leave Petition stands disposed of.

undertaking, in the usual form, shall be filed by the petitioners
within two (02) weeks from today, failing which the Registry shall
take appropriate steps.

have been made aware of the consequences of breach of such
undertaking(s), including initiation of contempt proceedings.
6. The arrears of rent due and payable, if any, shall be
positively cleared within three weeks from today.
7. Needless to add, till such time the petitioners occupy the
premises, they shall continue to pay occupational charges at the
same rate at which the rent was agreed to be paid.
8. Accordingly, the present Special Leave Petition is disposed
of.
